questions.q: What are the main steps of the foundation model workflow?
options: Pre-train on many series, then forecast new series from the context, optionally adapt.
Wait until the series is long.

questions.q: Which items are limits of a given model? Select all.
Your context has 3,000 points; the model reads 512. How many points does it use?
questions.why: It uses the most recent 512 points.

questions.q: A vendor says its model is 'the best on all data'. What is the right reaction?
options: Run your own backtest against baselines on your data.
why: Without your own evidence, it is a risk.

questions.q: You have 40,000 short series (30 points each) and no time to tune. Which approach is a sensible first try?
options: Zero-shot foundation model plus seasonal naive baseline, compared on a backtest.
why: Correct: short, many series is a good fit for zero-shot, and the baseline keeps you honest.

questions.q: The MASE of a model is 0.8 and its seasonal naive baseline has MASE 1.0 on the same series. What do you say?
options: The model is about 20% better than the baseline on this metric.

questions.q: Why must you pin the model version in production?
options: A new weights version can change every forecast without code changes.
